# Loyaltymaster Design System

> Canonical entry manifest for any LLM building Loyaltymaster.com pages from
> this repo. Read this file first. Every page must match the approved design
> system as it runs live on https://loyaltymaster.com — canonical examples:
> https://loyaltymaster.com/features/ and
> https://loyaltymaster.com/digital-loyalty-card-for-coffee-shops/
> (The original template page at sendpush.loyaltymaster.com was retired in
> July 2026 when the design system was rolled out onto loyaltymaster.com
> itself; that subdomain no longer resolves.)

## The Key Rule

Loyaltymaster pages must be built from approved components only. The AI may
compose approved Lego blocks; it may not invent new design — no new components,
variants, tokens, colors, radii, shadows, typography, layouts, animation, or
hover behavior. The rules live on three levels: brand rules (`BRAND.md`,
`DESIGN_SYSTEM.md`), component rules (`specs/components/*.md`), and combination
rules (`templates/*.md`).

The same rule applies to facts: the AI may draft copy in the `BRAND.md` voice,
but every fact, number, price, and claim must match the production facts canon
(see Content Authority below). No invented stats, testimonials, or offers.

## Pick Your Task

- Draft page outline (no code): follow `RUNBOOK_A_PAGE_TO_MARKDOWN_OUTLINE.md`.
  Output is Markdown only; a human must approve it before any code exists.
  `LLM_MARKDOWN_OUTLINE_PACK.md` is a copy-paste prompt wrapper for this mode.
- Approved outline → production page: follow
  `RUNBOOK_B_MARKDOWN_OUTLINE_TO_PRODUCTION_PAGE.md`.
- Missing component or template: stop and complete
  `templates/new-component-request.md`. Never improvise inside the artifact.

Each runbook embeds its own runtime read list — follow it. Core sources both
runbooks rely on:

- `registry/components.json` — the ONLY component inventory. Build the
  available component list from it at runtime. Never trust a component count
  or list written in prose docs; counts in older docs describe gating waves,
  not availability. Only `status: "stable"` components may be used.
- `tokens/design-tokens.json` — the only token source (DTCG JSON).
  `tokens.css`, `tokens.d.ts`, and `tailwind.preset.cjs` are generated exports
  (`node scripts/generate-tokens.mjs`).
- `specs/components/<id>.md` — read the current spec immediately before using
  a component.
- `templates/` — approved composition recipes per artifact type.
- `examples/approved/`, `examples/blocked/`, `examples/generated/` — accepted
  patterns, rejection patterns, and full proof packages.

## Content Authority

The production facts canon is `SOURCE-OF-TRUTH.md` in the production
repository (see Production Target below). Every fact the page states —
prices, plan names, offer story, turnaround times, stats, contact details,
legal claims — must match that file. Copy the fact; never restate it from
memory. A fact you cannot verify there goes into the outline as
`contentStillNeeded`, and Runbook B stops with `CONTENT_MISSING` until a
human resolves it.

## Production Target

Unless the task brief names a different repository, `{{TARGET_REPOSITORY}}`
is the Loyaltymaster production repo:

- Local path: `/Users/johs777/LOYALTYMASTER/Loyaltymaster Clone Codex`
- GitHub: `https://github.com/johs01/Loyaltymaster` (deployed to
  loyaltymaster.com via Vercel)

Runbook B documents the exact files a new page registers there. If the brief
names no target and that path is unavailable, produce the route-agnostic
package and record the target as UNKNOWN in the diagnostic report.

## Hard Boundaries

- Body-only by default: production supplies the global navbar/header/footer.
  `navbar-glassmorphism` and `footer` are shell-only exceptions for explicitly
  standalone artifacts.
- `/Components/` is evidence only (screenshots, handoff archives, source
  review). Runtime imports come exclusively from `library/src/components/` via
  each component's registry `libraryPath`.
- Read-only sources — never edit, import from, or copy runtime code from:
  `/Users/johs777/LOYALTYMASTER/sendPUSH-PRODUCTION`,
  `RAW/Pre-Flight - New Page Creation/sendPUSH-PRODUCTION/` (both are frozen
  replicas of the retired sendPUSH app), raw MagicPath output, and
  `_archive/`. The production repo named above is edited only when the task
  explicitly authorizes direct edits; otherwise emit an import-ready package.
- React is server-by-default; each component declares `clientBoundary` in the
  registry. Validation uses TypeScript types + JSON Schema (no Zod).

## Do Not Read (noise for page-generation tasks)

- `_archive/` — historical material, including phase reports and old design
  system versions. Exception: when a live doc (for example `PREFLIGHT.md` or
  `registry/README.md`) cites a specific archived phase report as frozen gate
  evidence, reading that cited file is allowed.
- `RAW/` — research captures and production replicas.
- `Claude Memory/` — internal session memory.
- `.understand-anything/`, `project-birds-eye-report/`, `.playwright-mcp/`,
  `.nested-git-backups/` — tooling output and backups.
- `showcase/app/artifacts/` and `showcase/preview/` — historical gate
  screenshots and logs. Exception: the specific JSON result ledgers a live
  doc names (for example `interaction-results.json`,
  `production-fidelity-results.json`) are readable gate evidence.

## Optional Reference

- `AI_START_HERE.md` — expanded workflow overview and proof-package index.
- `EXTERNAL_LLM_HANDOFF.md` — hand-off checklist for external agents.
- `PREFLIGHT.md` — the human-gated checklist a human reviewer completes
  before a new page is planned; LLMs follow the runbooks, which embed the
  same rules.
- `READ_FIRST_AI.md` — operating manual with gate evidence details.
- `KNOWN_ISSUES.md` — pre-existing deferred issues.

## Validation

After Runbook B output, run `node scripts/validate-phase2.mjs` and
`node scripts/validate-runbook-poc-readiness.mjs`, then record human approval
before publishing. When the target repo is available, also run its own checks
(`npm run check` and `npx vitest run` in the production repo).
